Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses TERMS & CONDITIONS Name of Work: Repair and Renovation of Room No. 22 of Main Office Building at ICAR-CIAH, Bi kaner. 1. Site Visit 1.1 The bidder shall visit the site before quoting to acquaint himself with the existing conditions, dimensio ns, accessibility, nature of work and site constraints. 1.2 No claim for extra payment or extension of time due to ignorance of site conditions shall be entertaine d after award of work. 1.3 All dimensions and site measurements shall be verified by the contractor before commencement of the work. 2. Completion Period 2.1 The entire work shall be completed within 60 (Sixty) days from the date of issue of the work order. 2.2 Time shall be the essence of the contract. 2.3 Delay in completion shall attract Liquidated Damages (LD) as per GeM Contract conditions and applica ble Government of India rules. 2.4 The contractor shall plan and execute the work in a systematic manner to minimise disturbance to the regular functioning of the Institute. 3. Scope of Contractor 3.1 The contractor shall execute all items covered under the BOQ and detailed Scope of Work, complete in all respects. 3.2 All necessary labour, materials, tools and plants, transportation, loading, unloading, installation access ories, consumables and other incidental requirements shall be arranged by the contractor. 3.3 Any minor item or incidental work necessary for satisfactory completion of the specified items shall be deemed included in the quoted rates, provided it does not constitute an additional or materially different it em of work. 3.4 The contractor shall coordinate with the Officer-in-Charge before commencing each stage of work. 4. Materials 4.1 All materials shall be new, unused, of approved make and quality and shall conform to relevant IS Cod es, CPWD Specifications and manufacturer's standards, wherever applicable. 4.2 All materials shall be got approved from the Officer-in-Charge before use. 4.3 No inferior, defective or substitute material shall be used without prior written approval of the Officer-i n-Charge. 4.4 The contractor shall produce manufacturer details, technical specifications, product literature and test

certificates wherever required by the Officer-in-Charge. 4.5 Any material found defective or not conforming to the approved specifications shall be removed and re placed by the contractor at his own cost. 5. Aluminium Framework Work 5.1 Aluminium sections shall conform to IS 733 and IS 1285, as applicable, and shall be of approved make and suitable dimensions. 5.2 Anodised aluminium sections shall have a minimum anodic coating of Grade AC 15 conforming to IS 18 68. 5.3 Aluminium sections shall be straight, smooth, rust-free and free from dents, bends or other manufactu ring defects. 5.4 All cutting, fabrication, mitring, drilling and jointing shall be carried out properly to ensure accurate di mensions and alignment. 5.5 Necessary EPDM/neoprene gaskets, cleat angles, snap beading, stainless steel/CP brass screws and oth er fixing accessories shall be provided wherever required. 5.6 The completed framework shall be properly secured, aligned and finished as per approved requirement s. 6. Aluminium ACP Cupboards 6.1 Aluminium cupboard shutters shall be fabricated using extruded aluminium sections of approved size a nd thickness with ivory-coloured powder-coated finish. 6.2 ACP sheets shall be 3 mm thick exterior-grade, of approved make, colour and finish, as specified in the BOQ. 6.3 ACP sheets shall be properly fitted within the aluminium framework without gaps, uneven edges or loose connections. 6.4 Necessary hinges, handles, magnetic catches, locks, screws and other fixing accessories shall be provi ded complete. 6.5 All cupboard shutters shall be properly aligned and shall operate smoothly without rubbing, sagging or misalignment. 6.6 The existing brick masonry cupboards shall not be damaged during installation. Any damage caused s hall be rectified by the contractor at his own cost. 7. PVC Rigid Foam Panelled Shutters 7.1 PVC rigid foam panelled shutters shall be factory-made, 30 mm thick, both-side laminated and conform ing to IS 4020, as specified in the BOQ. 7.2 The shutters shall be of approved make, colour and finish. 7.3 Necessary cutting, fitting, hinges, handles, screws and other accessories required for proper installatio n shall be provided. 7.4 The shutters shall be properly aligned and fixed to the existing cupboard/partition arrangement. 7.5 The finished shutters shall be free from cracks, dents, surface defects and uneven edges and shall ope rate smoothly. 8. Vinyl Flooring 8.1 Vinyl flooring shall be 2.0 mm thick cushion/flexible vinyl flooring conforming to IS 3462, of approved make, shade and pattern. 8.2 Existing Kota stone flooring shall be thoroughly cleaned before laying vinyl flooring. 8.3 The existing floor surface shall be checked and suitably prepared to ensure proper adhesion.

8.4 Vinyl flooring shall be fixed using approved rubber-based adhesive as per the manufacturer's recomme ndations. 8.5 The flooring shall be properly rolled using a light wooden roller to ensure uniform adhesion. 8.6 The finished flooring shall be free from air bubbles, wrinkles, loose edges, open joints or undulations. 8.7 Necessary cutting and finishing around walls, door frames and other obstructions shall be carried out n eatly. 9. Vertical Blinds 9.1 Vertical blinds shall be made of 300 GSM polyester fabric, waterproof and sun-blocking type, of approv ed make, colour and shade. 9.2 The blinds shall be manufactured according to the actual dimensions of the existing window. 9.3 The blinds shall be installed complete with headrail, brackets, operating mechanism, control cord/chai n and other necessary accessories. 9.4 The operating mechanism shall function smoothly and the fabric strips shall hang vertically in proper a lignment. 9.5 All fixing arrangements shall be secure and shall provide proper coverage of the window opening. 10. Aluminium Window Modification 10.1 The existing aluminium window shall be modified by changing the shutter opening direction from out ward to inward without damaging the existing frame. 10.2 Necessary dismantling, cutting, fabrication, welding, repositioning/refixing of hinges and other hardw are shall be carried out. 10.3 Necessary adjustments shall be made to ensure proper alignment and functioning of the shutter. 10.4 The modified window shall open and close smoothly without obstruction. 10.5 Any damage caused to the existing frame, adjoining wall or finish during modification shall be made good by the contractor at his own cost. 11. uPVC Sliding Wire-Mesh Window 11.1 The factory-made uPVC sliding window shall be of two-track, two-panel configuration, using R2 series profiles as specified in the BOQ. 11.2 The uPVC profiles shall conform to EN 12608 and applicable CPWD specifications, with minimum wall thickness of 1.70 mm for R2 series. 11.3 Necessary galvanised mild steel reinforcement shall be provided within the profiles as per approved design. 11.4 Sliding arrangements shall include aluminium roller track, wool pile, nylon rollers with SS 304 body an d suitable zinc alloy powder-coated touch locks with hook. 11.5 Necessary EPDM gaskets, SS 304 grade fasteners, interlocks, fixing accessories and other component s shall be provided complete. 11.6 Wire mesh shall be properly installed and securely fixed to provide effective insect protection while m aintaining ventilation. 11.7 The window frame shall be properly aligned, levelled and fixed in the existing opening. 11.8 The gap between the frame and adjoining wall shall be sealed using approved weatherproof silicone s ealant over suitable backer rod. 11.9 Sliding shutters shall move smoothly without obstruction, and the locking arrangement shall function properly.

11.10 The completed installation shall be tested for proper operation, alignment and stability. 12. Hydraulic Door Closers and Door Stopper 12.1 Hydraulic door closers shall be aluminium die-cast body tubular-type universal hydraulic closers conf orming to IS 3564, with ISI marking, suitable for the specified door weight and width. 12.2 Necessary mounting brackets, screws, arms and accessories shall be provided complete. 12.3 The hydraulic mechanism shall be properly adjusted to ensure controlled and smooth closing of the d oor without excessive impact. 12.4 The aluminium floor-mounted door stopper shall be ISI marked and anodised, conforming to IS 1868 with minimum Grade AC 10 coating. 12.5 The door stopper shall be securely fixed at a suitable location to prevent the door from striking adjoini ng walls or installations. 13. Painting 13.1 Existing wall and ceiling surfaces shall be properly cleaned and prepared before painting. 13.2 Loose, flaking or deteriorated paint shall be removed wherever necessary. 13.3 Necessary filling of minor cracks, nail holes and surface imperfections shall be carried out wherever r equired. 13.4 Acrylic smooth exterior paint of approved make and shade shall be applied over the existing cement- painted surface. 13.5 A minimum of two coats shall be applied to achieve uniform shade, adequate coverage and satisfacto ry finish. 13.6 The finished surface shall be uniform in shade without visible brush marks, roller marks, patches or st ains. 13.7 Existing flooring, doors, windows, cupboards, electrical fittings and other installations shall be adequa tely protected during painting. 14. Workmanship and Quality Control 14.1 All workmanship shall conform to applicable CPWD Specifications 2023, relevant IS Codes and good e ngineering practices. 14.2 All fabrication, installation, fixing and finishing works shall be carried out by skilled and experienced workers. 14.3 The Officer-in-Charge shall have the right to inspect the materials and workmanship at any stage of e xecution. 14.4 Any defective workmanship or installation not conforming to approved specifications shall be rectified by the contractor at his own cost. 14.5 Completion of any item shall be subject to satisfactory inspection and acceptance by the Officer-in-Ch arge. 15. Measurements and Payment 15.1 Payment shall be made only for the quantities actually executed, measured at site and accepted by t he Officer-in-Charge. 15.2 Measurements shall be recorded in accordance with applicable measurement rules and the relevant BOQ item descriptions. 15.3 No payment shall be made for defective, incomplete or rejected work. 15.4 No extra payment shall be admissible for materials, accessories or incidental operations already cove red under the respective BOQ items.

15.5 Payment shall be processed as per the terms and conditions of the GeM contract and applicable Instit ute procedures. 16. Safety 16.1 The contractor shall comply with all applicable safety regulations during execution. 16.2 Necessary personal protective equipment (PPE) shall be provided to all workers engaged at the site. 16.3 Proper precautions shall be taken during cutting, drilling, welding, fabrication, painting and other acti vities. 16.4 The contractor shall be solely responsible for any accident, injury or damage arising due to negligenc e on his part or that of his workers. 16.5 Electrical and other existing services shall be protected during execution. 17. Protection of Existing Property 17.1 Existing walls, flooring, furniture, electrical fittings, doors, windows and adjoining structures shall be adequately protected during execution. 17.2 The contractor shall take necessary precautions to avoid damage to existing building components an d Institute property. 17.3 Any damage caused during execution shall be rectified/repaired by the contractor at his own cost wit hout any additional payment. 18. Housekeeping and Disposal of Waste 18.1 The work area shall be kept neat and clean throughout the execution period. 18.2 All debris, dismantled materials, packing materials and construction waste shall be removed from the site. 18.3 No material or waste shall be stored in a manner that obstructs the normal functioning of the office. 18.4 On completion of work, the contractor shall thoroughly clean the room and hand it over in a neat and usable condition. 19. Taxes and Other Charges 19.1 The quoted rates shall be inclusive of all materials, labour, loading, unloading, transportation, tools a nd plants, scaffolding, consumables, overheads, contractor's profit and all incidental charges required for s atisfactory completion of the work. 19.2 GST shall be applicable as per prevailing Government of India rules and the GeM contract conditions. 19.3 The contractor shall be responsible for payment of all applicable taxes, duties and statutory charges, as per applicable laws. 20. Defect Liability Period 20.1 The Defect Liability Period (DLP) shall be 12 (Twelve) months from the date of satisfactory complet ion and handing over of the work. 20.2 During the DLP, the contractor shall rectify, at his own cost, any defect arising due to defective mater ials, poor workmanship, improper installation or faulty fabrication. 20.3 The defects covered shall include, but not be limited to, ACP cupboard shutters, aluminium framewor k, PVC shutters, vinyl flooring, vertical blinds, aluminium window modification, uPVC sliding wire-mesh win dow, painting and door accessories. 20.4 The contractor shall attend to reported defects within a reasonable period as directed by the Officer-i n-Charge. 20.5 Rectification of defects during the DLP shall be carried out without any additional financial liability to t

he Institute. 21. Officer-in-Charge 21.1 The Officer-in-Charge shall have the right to inspect and supervise the work at any stage of execution . 21.2 The decision of the Officer-in-Charge regarding quality, measurements, workmanship, materials and c onformity with the approved specifications shall be final, subject to the provisions of the contract. 21.3 The contractor shall comply with all reasonable instructions issued by the Officer-in-Charge regarding execution and completion of the work. 22. General Conditions 22.1 The contractor shall comply with all applicable statutory provisions, labour laws and directions issued by ICAR-CIAH during execution. 22.2 The Institute reserves the right to increase or decrease the quantities of any item, as per actual site r equirements and applicable GeM contract conditions, without changing the accepted unit rates, subject to permissible contractual limits. 22.3 The contractor shall not sublet the work without prior permission wherever such permission is require d under the contract. 22.4 The contractor shall maintain discipline and ensure that his workers do not cause inconvenience to In stitute employees or visitors. 22.5 Any matter not specifically covered herein shall be governed by the applicable GeM contract conditio ns, relevant CPWD Specifications and prevailing Government of India rules. 22.6 The contractor shall hand over the completed work in a neat, clean, fully functional and satisfactory c ondition. . 15.
